$comment: Model type: conceptual. This example is a technology-neutral conceptual model of a community library. It is represented as a blueprint with no implementation detail: the key business capabilities (Membership, Catalogue, Lending) are assets linked by typed relationships, and the core domain concepts (Member, Item, Branch, Loan) are data objects whose associations are expressed as data relationships with cardinality. There are deliberately no protocols, deployments, keys, or flows, which is what distinguishes a conceptual model from a logical or data-flow one.

blueprints.name: Community library conceptual model
blueprints.description: A technology-neutral conceptual model of a community library, capturing the key business concepts and how they relate, without any implementation detail such as databases, services, or protocols.

scope.name: Lending domain
scope.description: Concepts involved in lending physical items to members.

assets.name: Membership
assets.description: The capability concerned with enrolling and identifying members.

assets.name: Catalogue
assets.description: The capability concerned with describing and locating items.

assets.name: Lending
assets.description: The capability concerned with loans, due dates, and returns.

dataSets.name: Library domain entities
dataSets.description: The conceptual entities of the lending domain and their associations.

dataObjects.name: Member
dataObjects.description: A person enrolled to borrow items.

dataObjects.name: Item
dataObjects.description: A borrowable item such as a book or recording.

dataObjects.name: Loan
dataObjects.description: The act of a member borrowing an item for a period.

assumptions.description: An item belongs to exactly one branch at a time, though it may move between branches.
